newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end down on exports and fund selling.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end down on exports and fund selling.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed lower on a lower-than-expected export sales number for soybeans in USDA's weekly export sales report, traders said.
Fund selling, led by Smith Barney's sale of eight million bushels of November, led the declines, they said.
"People were disappointed in the bean sales. They were talking yesterday of maybe over one million tonnes but it didn't get there," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
USDA early Thursday said U.S. soybean net export sales during the week ended October 3 were at 582,400 tonnes.
Sales to China totaled 55,000 tonnes -- much less than industry watchers expected, traders said.
Position squaring was noted before the release at 0730 CDT Friday of USDA's crop production and supply/demand reports, the traders said.
An average of analysts' estimates placed the U.S. 1996 soybean production number at 2.287 billion bushels, above the government's September forecast for 2.270 billion.
November's relative strength index (RSI) dropped to 26.034 points, just below oversold status at 30.
Soybeans closed five to 9-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with November down eight at $7.30-1/4.
While some said the drop in soybeans was tied to exports, others cited technical reasons for the slide.
"I think it is a technical game and the market is just leaning the wrong way," said Doug Hjort, president of Iowa-based consulting firm, Hjort Associates.
"They were talking about the export number for beans being a million tonnes or more which is totally ridiculous since the Chinese sales haven't had time to get on the books yet," he said.

The rumors about Chinese demand for optional-origin soybeans and soymeal began to circulate late last week, after the October 3 USDA export reporting cutoff point. The China buying talk peaked Monday and soybeans spiked higher that day.
Soybean futures volume for Thursday was estimated at 43,000 contracts, up from 31,318 Wednesday, the CBOT said.

In soybean options, Farmers Commodities Corp bought 400 November $7.75 calls at 1-1/2 cents, Lind Waldock bought 450 January $7.00 puts at 5-1/2 cents and The Chicago Corp bought 400 November $7.75 puts at 8-1/2 cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 19,000, down from 20,181 Wednesday.
